# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 12 (Bi-Vb Pc12)

**Title (English, from literature):** Meeting a man in a concealed place

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 12, entitled *Paṭicchannokāsa* ("Meeting a man in a concealed place"), is an expiation rule for Buddhist nuns (*bhikkhunīs*) in the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule stipulates that a nun who, seeking privacy, stands alone with a man in a concealed place incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*). In her study of the nuns' legal corpus, Ute Hüsken analyzes Pācittiya 12 as part of a closely related cluster of rules (including Pācittiyas 11, 13, and 14) that regulate standing or conversing with a man in private or compromised locations [Hüsken 1997]. Hüsken notes that entering a concealed place functions as a preparatory act related to Pārājika 4 (where it constitutes a grave offense, *thullaccaya*), culminating in a *pācittiya* when a nun engages in conversation with a man there [Hüsken 1997]. She further observes an asymmetry with corresponding monks' rules, where standing is often exempted in circumstances where sitting together in seclusion is prohibited [Hüsken 1997].
